Yurgir is an Orthon, a powerful type of Fiend from the Nine Hells. He and his band of  Merregon Legionnaires are in the Gauntlet of Shar, where they have been trapped by consequence of a contract with  Raphael.
“
Bargaining are you? A Kara-Tur warlord once tried the same - I made him watch as I ate his concubines and young, then fashioned a codpiece from his skull.
„
— Yurgir

Overview

Background

Yurgir is an orthon who has been trapped in the Gauntlet of Shar for many years, unable to fulfil the requirements of his contract with Raphael. Under the devil's orders, he and his merregons devastated Ketheric Thorm's Dark Justiciars, killing all they found from the Grymforge to the Gauntlet.

Description

Yurgir is a towering and foreboding figure, a veteran of the Blood War who is confident in his command. He speaks in a low rumble, his skin hard and red with three large sets of horns curling from the crown of his head.

Yurgir loves a good fight, and has respect for capable warriors.

History

A long time ago, Yurgir fought on the front-lines of the Blood War.[1]

Sometime around the late 14th century DR,  Ketheric Thorm began amassing an army of  Dark Justiciars.  Morfred, a Selûnite mason who had worked for Ketheric, including creating Moonrise Towers,[2] had tried to build a resistance against him to no avail. He eventually contacted  Raphael, asking him to destroy Ketheric's army.[3] Raphael then recruited Yurgir and his band of  Merregon Legionnaires for this mission; Yurgir signed a contract with Raphael:

“
Spill all the blood sworn to the night.
Silence all prayers; smother each rite.

Wander Shar's halls; hungry to slay;
Leave no Justiciar alive to obey.

Leave none to hear it, then be set free;
This song is your oath, swear, swear to me.[4][5]
 „


His contract stated that he must fulfill its terms, die trying, or forfeit his freedom and become Raphael's slave. Yurgir carried out his attack with his legion of Merregons, breaking through the walls of the Grymforge and killing the Justiciar presence there.[6][7] He and his legion then moved to the Gauntlet of Shar to defeat the remaining Justiciars.

With no more Justiciars to be found, Yurgir and his band seemed to have succeeded. However, Yurgir remained bound to the Gauntlet. Unbeknownst to Yurgir, Raphael had given a book named  One Becomes Many to the final Dark Justiciar,  Lyrthindor, which helped him to escape through splitting his body into a swarm of rats.[8]

Unable to fulfill and unwilling to break his contract and enter into servitude, Yurgir remained in the Gauntlet, hunting shadows for a century.

Involvement

Act Two

While exploring the Gauntlet of Shar, the party is lured by  Nessa, a Displacer Beast, into an ambush with Yurgir and his Merregons.[9] Yurgir catches the scent of Raphael on them immediately and voices his hatred of the devil, explaining the details of their contract. As a result of the contract he intends to kill anyone that dare venture into his wing of the temple. The party can continue speaking to Yurgir to learn more about his circumstances and about the fate of the Dark Justiciars, and even agree to try and help free him. Proceeding through his encounter can go two ways: ⁠Kill Raphael's Old Enemy or ⁠Break Yurgir's Contract. If the party already killed  Lyrthindor, Yurgir does not attack the party and instead thanks them for their help.

Killing Yurgir

Bards and Warlocks are given a unique opportunity to defeat Yurgir and his group through dialogue checks. It is also possible for other classes if they pass a  DC 14 Insight Check check after Yurgir recites his contract.[10]

It is possible to gain several inspiration points while dealing with Yurgir:

  • ⁠Catchy Tune ( Entertainer background) - for listening to Yurgir recite his contract in song
  • ⁠Killer Poetry ( Haunted One background) - for tricking Yurgir to kill himself
  • ⁠Return to Sender ( Soldier background) - if Yurgir is killed
  • ⁠Strength in Cowardice ( Urchin background) - for convincing Yurgir to spare you, for now
  • ⁠Tools of the Trade ( Outlander background) - for obtaining Yurgir's  Hellfire Hand Crossbow
  • ⁠The Devil's in the Details ( Charlatan background) - for passing the Insight check to spot the issue with his contract

It is also possible to sneak up on Yurgir and his group, avoiding conversation entirely. Stealing from Yurgir's chests (such as using stealth) locks the party out of all friendly negotiations with him, even if the characters doing the stealing are not detected. Additionally, if the party attack Nessa before she lures them to Yurgir, this also prevents peaceful negotiation.

While in peaceful negotiations with Yurgir, the party can convince his displacer beast, Nessa to fight against him with a Persuasion check, after investigating the spider carcass.

Breaking Yurgir's contract

While exploring the Gauntlet of Shar, the party can discover the book  One Becomes Many at the foot of the large statue of  Shar. It reveals that the rats in the area are actually parts of the final Dark Justiciar, baited into splitting by Raphael.

The party can defeat the rats, and then  Lyrthindor, and return to Yurgir so that he and Raphael can renegotiate the terms of his employment. This can be done preemptively in which case Yurgir and all the Merregons turn friendly, even if not having talked to them yet. Immediately after finishing dialogue Yurgir returns to Raphael's House of Hope.[11]

Additionally, if  Astarion is present, he becomes upset that the party have not killed Yurgir and questions them. He is furious and asks why he should remain in the party at all. A  DC 14 Persuasion or Deception Check is required to convince him to remain in the party.[12]

Act Three

During ⁠Deal with the Devil in Act Three, the party can find  Raphael at Sharess' Caress, where he offers them a deal; the  Crown of Karsus in exchange for the means to free Prince  Orpheus.

Visiting camp

If the party freed Yurgir from his contract, the orthon appears one night during a Long Rest. He compliments the Campsite and tells the player character to seek out the diabolist  Helsik at the Devil's Fee in order to access Raphael's abode, the House of Hope. When questioned on his motives, Yurgir appears genuinely thankful for helping him with his contract and considers it a favour repaid.

House of Hope

Yurgir is encountered again while leaving the House of Hope after stealing from Raphael. In the ensuing fight, if the party helped free him from his contract, he switches allegiances and helps the party kill Raphael. If the party killed Yurgir in Act Two, he can still be persuaded to aid the party with a  DC 30 Persuasion Check. If the party performed the actions to free him of his contract, but do not go through the related dialogue, then it is still necessary to persuade Yurgir.

If Yurgir aids the party, he becomes an ally for ⁠Gather Your Allies. When summoned, he becomes an Attached Follower through the action  Hellstalker Yurgir.

  10. ↑ There is an Insight check during dialogue to figure out that the lyrics hide a trick, then a  DC 16 Persuasion Check to convince Yurgir to kill his minions, then a  DC 21 Persuasion Check to convince him to kill his Displacer Beast, then yet another  DC 21 Persuasion Check to convince him to kill himself. Even succeeding on just the first roll makes the fight significantly easier.
  11. ↑ It is still possible to kill Yurgir at this point, which also results in him returning to Raphael's House of Hope.
  12. ↑ Normally,  Astarion vehemently disapproves of any action where  Raphael has offered to reveal the meaning behind his scars but may do so not if the deal to kill  Yurgir is not fulfilled (for example, if Yurgir kills himself). However if Raphael never offers the deal, Astarion neither disapproves of the party striking a deal with Yurgir nor convincing him to kill himself. If Astarion is in the party and they seek to avoid Raphael offering the deal, Astarion must be  disguised when they encounter Raphael at the Last Light Inn and the entrance to the Grand Mausoleum, or far enough away to not be brought into these conversation cut-scenes with Raphael when they begin.
  13. ↑ If Yurgir is defeated in both Act Two and Act Three, the Hellfire Hand Crossbow can still only be looted once. If Yurgir is disarmed of both his melee and ranged weapons during his a fight, his weapons do not replenish during any subsequent fight where he appears, locking him out of any abilities associated with those weapons.
  14. ↑ During the fight against him in the Gauntlet of Shar, once he gets to low enough health he throws multiple Orthonic Handbombs all around him, all of which can be picked up and used as regular grenades.
